title: The Nature of Divine Correction
english: And the Sabbaths—these Sabbaths are shadowy. [Gapped] ... to have rest becoming the people of God. 'In remembrance concerning the Sabbath. Lord, do not reprove me in your anger' (Psalm 6:1). Thus the Sabbath was remembered, in which nothing is worshipped [Gapped] ... is led there, he remembers the most beautiful thing there [Gapped] ... they sing the psalm. He who sincerely repents [Gapped] ... for so shall sincere repentance be shown; [Gapped] ... it seems he does this hypocritically. It is necessary, therefore, to suppose such a repentance, so that its magnitude and its beauty may be seen.

2 Lord, do not reprove me in your anger, nor discipline me in your wrath (Psalm 6:1). [Gapped] ... then he offers [something] on account of sin. This is therefore what he says: 'I will be anxious concerning my sin' (Psalm 40:17). Because I am a sinner, discipline me. Having taken remembrance concerning his own sin, he says these things. [Gapped] ... he knows sin in one way, but in another way he does not understand it; for in the one way he has experience of it, he knows it, but he does not understand it. If he had understood that it is harmful and both destructive and brings the greatest loss, he would not have understood it [meaning: he would not have been subject to it]. Therefore, he is able to know it and yet not understand it, he who is taking experience of it while being outside of it. The man according to Jesus was said not to have known sin nor to have done it (Hebrews 4:15). According to the other meaning of 'to know,' no one more than he knew it; for how had he come to have known it? 'Lord, do not reprove me in your anger, nor discipline me in your wrath' (Psalm 6:1). [Gapped] ... to have the [Gapped].

An outcome: often an anger and a plague that comes upon someone shows that person's sin. He endured much impiety, and was delivered to the Assyrians, and to the Babylonians into their hand; for it did not happen that the handing over of Israel occurred by chance, but because of sins previously committed; 'Jerusalem has sinned a sin' (Ps 51:5), and it became a reproach. He sinned much sin, and not simply he sinned, but also 'a sin': 'Jerusalem has sinned a sin'.

Therefore, when someone falls into grievous reproaches because of sins previously committed. He did not say, therefore, 'do not rebuke me at once' nor 'do not discipline me at once', but 'all things being reproved are made manifest by the light'. The reproof through light through teaching happens. The holy person does not waive such a reproof.

Again, someone is being disciplined in anger, not knowing he has acted and thought badly. He wants to be reproved thus as it has been said. But this reproof is not of passion, but of perception, as it has been said. When the sin is made manifest and [the person is punished]. And that of passion is less, just as the reproof of painful discipline is less.

In the presence of those who have strayed through wickedness, he says: 'Lord, discipline us before the judgment comes upon us; reveal to us the continuing punishment, remove from us—do not bring the threats upon us in their actual operation—and [let us be] in judgment, reveal to us even clearly what is to be done. The priests profane the Sabbath in the temple and are without cause [guilty]'. In such a way it is profaned, they are said to [do so] because of working...
